F1 22 with RT on is in the rasterization benchmarks and RT benchmarks. XT Significantly faster with RT off and beating the 4080.

"A 4070 Ti should cost no more than $700". The 2070 Super cost $500. The 3070 cost $500 (MSRP at least, we all know what happened). The generational uplift that Ampere provided was 30% over the 2070 Super. For the SAME PRICE. The 4070 Ti provides 50% uplift over the 3070 Ti in both 1440p and 4k, sure. But even if the card cost $700 more, that would be 40% more money. That's not progress, that's actually REGRESSION. But it doesn't cost $700, it costs $800. Meaning you have to pay 60% more money. The problem isn't that the cards are bad. The cards are okay. The problem is that I feel, as a consumer, that I'm just shoveling money into nothing.

Example: I'm rocking a 1080 Ti which I paid 750€ for just as the 2080 launched in Sept 2018. I'm willing to shell out 800€ for a GPU in 2023 again. What are my options? Hm... let's see. New first. I can get a new 6750XT for 750€. That doesn't feel great. I can get a 3060 Ti for 700€. I've fallen from the "one-below flagship" class to the "one above entry-level" class now?! That feels awful. I can get a new 3070, so there's 30% more performance for the same money. Not bad, but not great. I can get a used RTX 3080 for around 700€ in my country, and that would net me 60% more performance. That feels great. I'm paying less and getting more. OR, I can pay 1000€ (what 4070 Ti's are actually going for in Europe) so I can get an additional 27% more performance, but I need to pay 42% more money. That feels like shit. I'm paying way more, and getting not nearly as much. Where's the VALUE?!?!

comments.text:
@Katze822228  Bit of a fallacy here.  People who upgrade their monitors need them.  People who get used to 120Hz need them.  People playing modern games need them.

120Hz+ monitors have gotten so cheap and readily available, any new monitor people buy will be 120Hz, and at least 1440p.  That drives GPU requirements up.

Additionally, games are releasing unoptimized as hell, with some targeting brute force hardware if they aren't amateurishly designed (most Unity devs).   Lack of FSR/DLSS is still a big problem, and can only workaround bad design so much (Stranger of Paradise, for example).  Even 4080's can struggle in games that seem simple to run, solely due to this issue.

I upgraded my monitor in 2019 for christmas, expecting to go from a 1080 Ti to a 3080/Ti.  That never happened because of the pandemic and shortage and scalping.  I'm still on the 1080 Ti, it can barely run any modern game at 3440x1440 above 60FPS (HZD can't even reach 60 at medium settings), and 60FPS is unacceptable after even just a few months of 120Hz usage; it feels like how 30FPS used to.

The GPU and game industry is atrocious in every conceivable way right now.  I don't think a big crash/depression will happen again like in the past, but I wouldn't be surprised if one does.. and I'd welcome it.

comments.text: Looks like Ada (should be called Lovelace — sexist to use first names of female scientists while using last names of male scientists) is going to be Ampere pricing with better market conditions, meanwhile AMD is less competitive at launch with RDNA 3. Fire sale RDNA 2 is unmatched in its value right now. If AMD improves RDNA 3 drivers such that their cost per frame in Halo and Forza is average for them, and if AMD can halve idle power consumption, then I think the current price of the 7900 XTX is justified, and $800 would be justified for the 7900 XT. Until they do, the 4090 at MSRP (very hard to find) remains the only real winner so far this generation, and again, fire sale RDNA 2 is where it’s at, but that is disappearing fast. I believe both Nvidia and AMD are price fixing this generation, and my hope is that AMD lowers prices and Nvidia releases better value SKUs (their typical respective strategies) as soon as last-gen stock sells through. It was refreshing to see even a small drop in MSRP out of Nvidia, even masked as it was by a name change, but it’s not enough to make the 4070 Ti a winner on its own. It needs another $100 off. The 3070 and 3080 at MSRP two years ago were examples of Nvidia giving gamers impossibly little RAM at new high prices, justified by big performance gains, and Ada is the same VRAM skimping with no cost per frame gains, while their central marketing feature, DLSS frame generation, is in a better state than RTX and DLSS at Turing’s launch, but not yet mainstream or ready. It’s featured or going to be featured in two games I play, and their performance is already good enough I don’t need it. I can’t say Nvidia isn’t competitive at the price points 40 series cards currently occupy, but I can say that you shouldn’t buy at those price points right now because a $540 6800 XT is often close to a 4070 Ti with more RAM for 30% less money.
